candidates.description: A weaponized IMG shortcut launches VBS, executes PeppyRAT, profiles the host, persists in the startup folder and retrieves a second-stage DLL.

actions.name: Launch VBS from IMG shortcut

launching a Visual Basic script called doc.vbs

actions.name: Execute decoy PDF and PeppyRAT
actions.description: Display the decoy while executing the PeppyRAT Windows binary.

evidence.quote: identify it as a Python/PeppyRAT
ServiceHub.MsDetouredHost.exe
The infection chain continues executing both the decoy PDF document and a Windows PE (ServiceHub.MsDetouredHost.exe – 68d73d596a7103e517967f7f4e22cecb)

actions.name: Drop embedded Python runtime into TEMP
actions.description: Prepare the embedded Python execution environment.

evidence.quote: Python functions contained in the Python27.dll library
dropping all python compiled objects and dynamic-link libraries required into %TEMP% directory

actions.name: Enumerate processes and report to C2
actions.description: Collect the running-process list and send it to command and control.

evidence.quote: notifying the command-and-control server through an HTTP POST request
obtaining the list of running processes and notifying the command-and-control server through an HTTP POST request

actions.name: Create startup-folder persistence
actions.description: Drop a PE into the current user's startup folder.

evidence.quote: devenv.defender.scr
*simplify* function drops a new Windows PE file into the current user startup folder: (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\devenv.defender.scr)

actions.name: Receive next-stage DLL from C2
actions.description: Wait for and retrieve the next infection module.

evidence.quote: a DLL file named mscontainer.dll
waiting to receive a new infection module from the C2C, which is a DLL file named mscontainer.dll
The infection chain continues executing both the decoy PDF document and a Windows PE
dropping all python compiled objects and dynamic-link libraries required into %TEMP% directory, it makes this python command execution technique possible

Once the threat gets its environment all set, it builds and loads into memory a Python script that will be in charge of obtaining the list of running processes and notifying the command-and-control server through an HTTP POST request
Finally, as a persistence mechanism, *simplify* function drops a new Windows PE file into the current user startup folder
This later artifact has been developed in .NET framework and its purpose is very simple: waiting to receive a new infection module from the C2C, which is a DLL file named mscontainer.dll
this infection campaign seems to be related to the threat group Transparent Tribe
